settings.heroTitle: The best UAE business cards and spend tools, ranked by what each does best.
settings.heroLede: Four top-ten lists: corporate cards, spend management, international payments, and cashback and rewards. Ranked on published terms, with the reasoning shown.
settings.trust1: Ranked on what providers publish, with the reasoning shown
settings.trust2: A different provider can win each list
settings.trust3: You sign up with the provider, never with us
settings.noticeText: Information comes from provider websites and third-party reviews, last checked 22 Oct 2026. Rankings are our reading of published terms, not hands-on tests, and providers may change them. Confirm current terms before you sign up.
settings.footerNote: Jazaa is a comparison service. It is not a bank, card issuer or payment provider. © 2026
settings.bestText: A different provider can win each list. Every pick shows its reasoning and who else is worth a look.
settings.compareText: Open a list for the full ranking, or use the overview to see every provider at once. Tick two or three to compare them in detail.
settings.how1Text: Pricing, product and help pages first, then reputable third-party reviews. The check date and sources are shown for every provider.
settings.how2Title: We rank each list on stated criteria
settings.how2Text: Every list shows its criteria, in order of importance. We don’t pick one provider to win everything.
settings.how3Title: You sign up with the provider
settings.how3Text: Jazaa is a comparison service. It doesn’t issue cards, move money or guarantee approval.

features.name: Corporate cards
features.blurb: How many cards you can issue, which types, and what they cost.
features.criteria:
Cost and number of cards you can issue
Card types: virtual, physical, single-use, credit and prepaid
Spend controls on each card
Clarity of published terms
features.why: Alaan says it issues unlimited physical and virtual cards at no extra cost, with Apple Pay support. Few rivals publish both unlimited physical and unlimited virtual issuance.
features.notes: Pemo is close, with four card types, though one version of its plan table limits physical cards on lower tiers. Qashio, Wio Business and the banks offer credit cards, which suit larger limits.

alts.label: Best if you want a credit card with cashback
Best if you also collect customer payments

features.name: Spend management
features.blurb: Approvals, receipts, controls, VAT and accounting integrations.
features.criteria:
Receipt capture, approvals and policy controls
Accounting and ERP integrations, including VAT handling
Breadth: invoices, payables, petty cash, reimbursements
Pricing transparency
features.why: Pemo publishes the widest set of spend tools in one product: AI receipt matching, multi-layer approvals, VAT visibility, accounting sync, invoice management and a free starter tier.
features.notes: The top four are close. Pluto adds payables, petty cash and procurement, Alaan pairs AI coding with ERP integrations, and Qashio publishes the most per-card accounting controls.

alts.label: Best for large ERP setups such as SAP, Oracle and NetSuite
Best if you also need payables and petty cash
Best low-cost option for small teams

features.name: International payments
features.blurb: Paying suppliers and spending abroad: fees, currencies and countries.
features.criteria:
Published cost of international payments and FX
Currencies and countries covered
Foreign-currency accounts and hedging
FX terms on cards
features.why: Pluto is the only provider here that publishes free international payments (150+ countries, 140+ currencies) together with no card FX fee and cashback on foreign spend.
features.notes: ‘Free’ carries terms, so check limits and the rate used. Hubpay is a cross-border specialist with 30+ currency IBANs and FX hedging, but publishes no prices. Wio publishes explicit SWIFT fees.

alts.label: Best for regular supplier payments and FX hedging
Best for receiving client and marketplace payments
Best for clear, published SWIFT fees

features.name: Cashback and rewards
features.blurb: Cashback rates, caps, and what the rewards can be exchanged for.
features.criteria:
Cashback rate on international and UAE spend
Caps and conditions
Redemption options: cash, miles, points
Availability and eligibility
features.why: Qashio publishes uncapped cashback on both international (up to 2%) and UAE (up to 1%) spend, plus points that convert to cash or to Skywards, Shukran and Avios miles.
features.notes: Alaan lists similar rates without the miles option. Wio’s flat 2% beats both on UAE spend up to its monthly cashback cap, but it is a credit product by application.

alts.label: Best flat rate on smaller UAE spend
Best if your team flies Emirates

providers.name: Alaan
providers.tagline: Corporate cards with AI expense coding
providers.price: Free starter plan reported. Paid plans on request.
providers.d_cards: Says it issues unlimited prepaid physical and virtual cards instantly at no extra cost. Cards work with Apple Pay.
providers.d_spend: Automated receipt collection and categorisation, approval policies and VAT workflows, with integrations to QuickBooks, Sage, MS Dynamics, NetSuite and Xero.
providers.d_intl: Manages non-AED spend such as AWS, Meta and LinkedIn in one place with cashback. A Hubpay executive says the two have partnered on cross-border transfers.
providers.d_cashback: Kredit’s 2025 review lists 2% international and 1% domestic, both unlimited. Alaan’s own pages say up to 2% uncapped, sometimes on all card spend and sometimes on foreign-currency spend.

providers.name: Bayzat
providers.tagline: HR, payroll and finance in one platform
providers.d_cards: Bayzat’s card page lists unlimited cards with limits, approvers and cost centres. A finance page still labels cards as coming soon, so confirm availability.
providers.d_spend: Approved expenses flow into payroll, with custom approval chains, OCR receipt capture and mobile submissions. Out-of-policy card spend can be recovered on payroll.
providers.d_intl: Multi-currency accounts, global payments and accounts payable with lower FX rates, and same-day remittance. Rates aren’t published.
providers.d_cashback: Bayzat doesn’t publish a cashback or rewards programme.

providers.name: Emirates NBD
providers.price: Annual fees vary by card, so check with the bank.
providers.d_cards: Offers business credit cards plus Visa and Mastercard corporate cards. One review lists an annual fee of AED 1,500 with waivers tied to spend, and suggests it suits established companies.
providers.d_cashback: The Business Rewards card earns 2 points per $5 on Emirates bookings, 1 per $5 on general spend and 0.25 per $5 on utilities, government and education, with no monthly cap (Kredit, 2025).

providers.name: greytHR
providers.tagline: HR and payroll with an expense module
providers.price: From about USD 80/month for 25 employees, per greytHR.
providers.d_spend: AI receipt capture, multi-level approvals and policy rules, with approved expenses flowing into payroll. Free trial available. Not a card programme.

providers.name: Hubpay
providers.tagline: UAE cross-border payments and corporate FX
providers.d_intl: UAE-licensed platform with named IBANs in 30+ currencies, corporate FX with forward contracts and hedging, international payroll and payment links, plus an Africa collect-and-remit service.

providers.name: Mamo
providers.tagline: Payments and corporate cards in one account
providers.price: Free entry plan. Extra cards cost AED 19/month each, AED 9 on Growth, and are free on the top plan.
providers.h_cards: Visa credit and debit, unlimited on top plan
providers.d_cards: Physical, virtual, debit and credit cards, with card APIs. One free card on the entry plan, three on Growth, unlimited free on the top plan.
providers.h_spend: Free expense tools and instant top-ups
providers.d_spend: Real-time dashboard, limits per card and free expense management tools, with cards topped up from payments you collect through Mamo.
providers.d_intl: No foreign-transaction fee on cards, though standard exchange rates apply. International ATM withdrawals cost AED 20. You can collect in non-AED currencies and settle in AED or USD.
providers.d_cashback: Premium plan: 2% non-AED and 0.5% AED, uncapped. Growth plan: 1% and 0.4%. New card users get 8% for the first 3 months.

providers.name: Payoneer
providers.price: No monthly fee typically. An annual fee applies if you receive under USD 6,000 in 12 months.
providers.d_intl: Receiving accounts in 22 currencies, including AED, and payments from clients in 190+ countries across 70+ currencies. Fees vary by currency and method and show in your account. Client card payments can cost up to 3.99%.

providers.name: Pemo
providers.tagline: Cards, expenses and accounting in one platform
providers.price: Free Starter plan. Premium AED 399/month per company. Enterprise from AED 1,500/month.
providers.d_cards: Mastercard virtual, physical, single-use and pre-funded cards issued by NymCard, with Apple, Google and Samsung Pay. One version of its plan table limits physical cards on lower tiers.
providers.h_spend: AI receipts, approvals and accounting sync
providers.d_spend: AI receipt matching, multi-layer approval workflows, VAT visibility, spend limits per card and per purchase, accounting sync and invoice management.
providers.d_intl: Lists international cards for employees outside the UAE. Pemo’s pricing page doesn’t publish FX fees.
providers.d_cashback: Up to 2% cashback on business transactions, with the highest rate on paid plans. Also lists discounts on 100+ software tools and travel perks.

providers.name: Pluto
providers.price: Free plan reported for up to 5 card users. Paid tiers on request.
providers.d_cards: Virtual and physical cards with per-card budgets and category limits, usable wherever Visa or Mastercard is accepted.
providers.d_spend: Corporate cards, reimbursements, accounts payable, petty cash and procurement in one platform, with direct accounting sync such as Wafeq.
providers.d_intl: Advertises free international payments to 150+ countries and wires in 140+ currencies. A 2023 company announcement also says there is no FX fee on card spend.
providers.d_cashback: Unlimited cashback of up to 2% on spend in 100+ currencies. Pluto’s pages mark the rate with a footnote, so read the terms.

providers.name: Qashio
providers.tagline: Corporate cards with ERP-ready spend management
providers.price: Free Starter plan. Paid plans are listed on qashio.com/pricing.
providers.h_cards: Visa cards, unlimited on top plans
providers.d_cards: Prepaid Visa cards issued by NymCard, virtual or physical. Cards per user: 2 on Starter, 5 on Premium, unlimited on Business+. A third-party review also lists a Qashio credit card with limits up to AED 1 million.
providers.d_spend: Purchase, merchant and category limits per card, chart-of-accounts mapping per card, and integrations including NetSuite, SAP, Xero, Zoho, Odoo and Oracle.
providers.d_intl: Wallets in USD, EUR, GBP and SAR. Qashio describes its FX rates as low but doesn’t publish a figure.
providers.h_cashback: Up to 2% international, up to 1% UAE
providers.d_cashback: Uncapped, per Qashio’s offer page. Qashio Points convert to cashback (300 points for AED 10) or to Emirates Skywards, Shukran and Avios miles.

providers.name: QuickBooks
providers.d_spend: Imports bank and card transactions, matches receipts and categorises with AI assistance. Multi-level approvals are limited and claims need the Advanced plan, per greytHR’s review.

providers.name: RAKBANK
providers.d_cards: The Titanium Business Credit Card is described as free for life, with a credit card cheque facility.
providers.h_cashback: Up to 1%, capped at AED 1,000 a month
providers.d_cashback: Up to 1% on general domestic and international retail spend (to AED 1,000 a month) and 0.25% on categories such as government, bills, education, telecom and fuel. Redemption threshold AED 100.

providers.name: Wio Business
providers.price: Plans: Essential AED 99/month, Grow AED 249/month. Credit card by application.
providers.d_cards: Wio Business Credit offers a credit card with 2% cashback on everything. Wio says a credit decision takes up to three business days.
providers.d_intl: Free multi-currency accounts in AED, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD and CHF. SWIFT transfers cost AED 52.50 on Essential or AED 26.25 on Grow, plus correspondent bank fees. AED to USD is guaranteed at 3.673.
providers.h_cashback: 2% flat, up to AED 2,000 a month
providers.d_cashback: 2% cashback on everything, capped at AED 2,000 of cashback each month, which is about AED 100,000 of spend.

providers.name: Xpence
providers.d_cards: Issues virtual and physical Visa cards to employees with individual spending controls and limits, per its UAE launch coverage.
providers.d_spend: Automated receipt capture and categorisation, digital invoicing and automated bookkeeping. AI categorisation is claimed. Pricing isn’t published.
providers.d_intl: Multi-currency wallets alongside cards, per launch coverage. FX terms aren’t published.
providers.d_cashback: Xpence doesn’t publish a cashback or rewards programme.

providers.name: Zoho Expense
providers.tagline: Expense reports, budgets and card reconciliation
providers.price: Free for 3 users. Standard AED 11/user/month billed annually (AED 18 monthly). Premium AED 22 (AED 33 monthly).
providers.h_spend: Free for 3 users, with VAT tracking
providers.d_spend: Receipt autoscan, VAT tracking, corporate card management and reconciliation, multi-level approvals and budgets. A reporting and reimbursement tool rather than a card issuer.

faqs.a: An independent comparison of UAE business cards and spend tools. It lines up what providers publish about corporate cards, spend management, international payments and cashback.

faqs.q: How do you decide who is best?
faqs.a: Each list has stated criteria, shown in order of importance. We compare what providers publish against those criteria. A pick is our reading of published information, not a hands-on test, and it can change when providers update their plans.

faqs.q: Why isn’t one provider first everywhere?
faqs.a: Because the lists measure different things. A provider that leads on cashback may not lead on international payments. Each list also names who is best for specific situations.
Yes. Browsing and comparing is free. You sign up directly with the provider you choose.

faqs.q: Why does a provider say a rate is not published?
faqs.a: Some providers don’t list a figure on their public pages, or list it differently in different places. We say so rather than guess. Ask the provider for the current number.
